summary: Validated the redesigned Deloitte-style QBR PPTX export end-to-end. Backend GET /api/export/pptx returns a valid 9-slide deck for quarterly/monthly/weekly for tenant_id=all, both with data (uploaded XSOAR CSV) and empty state (N/A placeholders). Cover contains tenant name, 'Quarterly SOC Services Report' and 'Deloitte.' wordmark. Both section dividers ('Executive Summary', 'Incident Monitoring') are present. Exec Overview populated with SLA 71.4%, MTTR 0.5h, MTTD 12.6 min (numbers, not all N/A). Log-source distribution and MITRE tactic breakdown reflect the uploaded data. Frontend Export PPTX button on SOC Manager page triggers a valid .pptx download (43KB). Data cleaned up via DELETE /api/dashboard/soc-manager/data.
critical_code_review_comments: pptx_export.py is now 1900+ lines; consider splitting the legacy consulting-deck helpers from the QBR builders into separate modules for maintainability.
_num() helper in pptx_export.py has a slightly unusual boolean-precedence expression ('or' vs 'and') that could confuse future readers; consider parenthesizing explicitly.
seed_data_creation: Sample XSOAR CSV (7 incidents) uploaded to tenant_id=all during tests; cleaned up in final test via DELETE /api/dashboard/soc-manager/data?tenant_id=all.
context_for_next_testing_agent: QBR PPTX regression suite lives at /app/backend/tests/test_qbr_pptx.py — run with: python -m pytest backend/tests/test_qbr_pptx.py -o addopts= . The build_pptx() flow assembles exactly 9 slides in order: cover, section01, exec_overview, exec_performance, section02, log_sources, alerts, mitre, closing. Data source: all_data['soc_live'] (compute_soc_manager) + all_data['qbr'] (compute_qbr) + all_data['ti_live'] + all_data['rules_count']. Empty-state renders N/A placeholders correctly.
